en.name: Daniel Comboni
en.summary: Italian missionary bishop to central Africa who pioneered a strategy of training and empowering African clergy rather than relying solely on foreign missionaries.
en.body: Daniel Comboni volunteered as a young priest for the extremely demanding and dangerous central African mission field, where tropical disease had killed the overwhelming majority of earlier European missionaries within a few years of their arrival. Having witnessed this devastating attrition firsthand, he developed and promoted a missionary strategy summarized in his own phrase "Save Africa through Africa," emphasizing the training of local African clergy, catechists, and religious who could sustain the Church far more effectively and sustainably than a constant stream of foreign missionaries succumbing to disease, an approach considered visionary for its time and still influential in mission theology. As the first Vicar Apostolic of Central Africa, he founded schools and mission stations across the region and was also an outspoken opponent of the slave trade still active in parts of Sudan during his lifetime. He died in Khartoum in 1881, worn down by decades of harsh conditions and repeated bouts of illness, and was canonized in 2003.
